antecedent_conditions: Person P has occupied space S for extended period (months/years). Processing of S is fully habituated — Type 1 autopilot, no salience detection, S is "invisible." At time t, an event triggers re-seeing: (a) a visitor comments on S, (b) P returns to S after an absence, (c) a physical change occurs in S, (d) P's mood/stress state shifts.
predicted_outcome:
- Re-seeing triggers salience network activation (AI/dACC).
- CEN engages: P explicitly attends to features of S that had been habituated.
- Evaluation of S may be more positive than during habituation (if re-seeing reveals previously unappreciated qualities) or more negative (if re-seeing reveals previously unnoticed deficiencies).
- The re-seeing event produces a temporary spike in frontal theta, pupil dilation, and exploratory eye movement (reduced fixation predictability).
- Duration of re-seeing: brief (minutes to hours) before re-habituation begins.
architectural_consequence: Environments that support periodic re-seeing maintain higher long-term occupant satisfaction. Design strategies: seasonal variation in daylight, living elements that change (plants, water), material patina that evolves, spaces with "hidden" features revealed by changing light conditions or extended exploration.
name: Habituation Breakage and Re-Seeing
